In the third installment of a series about reading the Bible, a Catholic writer describes being horrified by the story of Lot and the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah in Genesis. The writer struggles to reconcile the story's violence and punishment with the God they have known and prayed to for nearly 42 years. Unsure how to interpret the account, the writer says their faith does not embrace such a punitive God. Despite these unresolved questions, they intend to continue reading.

Warnock dashed from his car and scrambled up a hill to the Yukon and its driver, 23-year-old Matthew Sitko, who appeared to be in shock. Warnock then reached in and pulled Sitko out to safety -- a moment recorded by Kough's camera. Thanks to Warnock, Sitko went to the hospital with just minor injuries.

After his Lucille Ball statue in Celoron, New York, drew widespread online attention over the weekend, Dave Poulin apologized for its disturbing appearance in a Monday letter to The Hollywood Reporter and offered his own time and money to remake it, expressing confidence he could do better after ten years. Mayor Scott Schrecengost rejected the offer as too late and said the town was seeking another sculptor to rework the head, neck and shoulders.

Two Transportation Security Administration screeners have been fired after conspiring to grope attractive men at Denver International Airport, Denver police said. Police say the female officer would tell the screening machine that a female passenger -- not a male -- was walking through, triggering an anomaly in the groin area and prompting the male officer to pat down the passenger. Investigator Chris Higgins watched the plan being carried out on February 9 and interviewed the female TSA officer, who said she had done this with her colleague at least 10 other times, police said. But it's unlikely criminal charges will be filed because there is no identifiable victim.
